event.summary: Deleted replay limits guarded only the removed byte-stream accumulator
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: removing the replay byte/frame constants does not remove any limit from the surviving grid path. Details: source check against the parent revision terminal.js:5718–5764 shows if(grid) receiveGrid(bytes) and return at 5738–5741, before byte replayChunks accumulation and both deleted limit checks at 5742–5760. Parent receiveGrid at 6188–6200 explicitly did not count grid data against these limits. The new component uses the same grid receive path (terminal.js:4165 onward; createGridSurface:4294 onward), with no replayChunks accumulation. Thus the suspected new resource-exhaustion consequence has no changed causal route in the assigned deletion: both caps only bounded a retired byte implementation. This is a source refutation of the removal premise, not a proof that every grid decoder limit is correct. Suggested bucket: other; no established security or loss-of-work impact. Confidence: confirmed source comparison, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation above. possible_cover: none searched. Could-be-highest: no established route from this deletion; the earlier trust-boundary concern was checked by tracing the pre-existing branch that bypassed these constants. Lead closed as candidate; no missing premise remains for this assigned change.

event.summary: Deleted replay limits guarded only the removed byte-stream accumulator
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: deleting the byte replay caps does not newly expose the grid path to unbounded hidden replay accumulation. Original suspected consequence preserved: a hostile or broken remote peer could exhaust page memory or leave it unusable; a security-impacting denial of service was not ruled out in the initial lead and remains a potentially-highest consequence for independent checking of this proposed refutation. Parent terminal.js:5738–5741 dispatched grid frames and returned before the deleted byte replayChunks accumulation and limits at 5742–5760. Parent receiveGrid:6188–6200 did not apply those limits to grid data. Current terminal.js:4466–4475 still hands frames to grid.receive and rearms only the idle timer. Synthesis checked grid-terminal.js:1973–1994: frames are decoded/applied immediately, but history may queue for sliced application; therefore the header's no-backlog explanation is not a claim that no history queue exists. grid-model.js:876–905 rejects malformed envelopes, does not enqueue empty appends, and trims real queued rows; 930–955 caps those rows at historyCap and discards superseded queue storage; 971–1007 validates retained rows on drain and caps applied history. The configured history cap and decoder dimensions/messages remain separate format bounds, not substitutes for every possible resource budget. No byte accumulation removed here ever guarded these grid allocations. Suggested bucket: other as refuted changed-route regression; original potentially security-impacting consequence retained. Confidence: confirmed source comparison, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation only, not accepted by parent. possible_cover: none searched. Could-be-highest: yes for the original hypothetical hostile-peer resource-exhaustion consequence; no changed route established by deleting these byte-only guards. This is not a blanket safety finding for the grid decoder, maximum legal history sizes, browser WebSocket buffering or pre-existing queue costs. No unresolved premise remains about what the deleted guards protected. Parent reports g083 independently agrees on pre-grid dispatch ordering; this conclusion relies on this group's own source reads and does not certify g083 delivery.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: the renamed sanitizer does not weaken protection against an embedded end-of-paste marker turning the rest of a paste into typed commands. Details: terminal.js:1908–1912 calls farhelmPasteSanitizer.sanitizePastedText in the same insertion path. The complete new paste-sanitizer.js function has exactly the same text.replace(/\x1b\[201~|\x1b/g, '') expression as the parent's term-bytes.js sanitizer; no semantic change. terminal.js:3203–3220 gates mounting on the new global, and createGridSurface:4354 supplies the same function for the grid's own paste handling. Suggested bucket: other (refuted regression). Confidence: confirmed source comparison, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation; both old and new functions remove the embedded terminator and remaining ESC bytes identically. possible_cover: none searched. This does not claim a general audit of all paste encoding.

Synthesis check: supervisor grid_input.rs:223–250 wraps each multipart paste once using the mode captured at its start; PasteText at 570–655 independently applies the same ESC/end-marker filter across parts before line-ending conversion. This supports only the changed sanitizer/dependency route and does not certify every possible paste-input policy. Suggested bucket: other as refuted regression; underlying hypothetical security/loss-of-work consequence remains preserved for independent check. Confidence: confirmed from source, not runtime. proposed_drop: source refutation, not accepted by parent; unchanged browser sanitization remains wired and downstream encoding sanitizes too. possible_cover: none searched. event.summary: Removing the xterm clipboard provider does not expose clipboard reads
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: removal of the old clipboard-read refusal does not let terminal programs read the user's system clipboard. Details: assigned patch deletes the ClipboardAddon provider because its xterm consumer is removed. Surviving createGridSurface onClipboard at terminal.js:4319–4331 writes only, through enqueueClipboardWrite at 764–773 (native write or navigator.clipboard.writeText); grid programs receive no browser clipboard reader. The emulator fixes osc52: Osc52::OnlyCopy in crates/farhelm-terminal-emulator/src/emulator.rs:99–105, queries.rs:360–362 documents clipboard_load as unanswered, and effects.rs:185–192 discards any ClipboardLoad event. SPEC.md Terminal experience:3060–3064 requires that OSC 52 READ never receives contents; replacement satisfies it by refusing upstream. Suggested bucket: other, refuted security regression. Confidence: confirmed source analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation; deletion removes an unused byte renderer's provider while the grid has write-only callbacks and emulator-side read refusal. possible_cover: none searched. Could-be-highest: clipboard exfiltration would be highest, but source rules out its premise in the replacement path. Browser user-initiated paste remains intentional and is independent of program queries.

event.summary: Removing the xterm clipboard provider does not expose clipboard reads
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: deleting the old renderer's clipboard-read refusal does not newly permit terminal programs to obtain system clipboard contents. Original potentially-highest consequence preserved: clipboard exfiltration could expose credentials or other private user data. Initial source checks: terminal.js:4319–4331 onClipboard only invokes writes through enqueueClipboardWrite:764–773, and the grid has no replacement browser clipboard query callback. Emulator configuration fixes osc52: Osc52::OnlyCopy (farhelm-terminal-emulator/src/emulator.rs:99–105); effects.rs:185–192 discards any ClipboardLoad event; queries.rs:360–362 documents unanswered clipboard loads. Synthesis resolved the configuration's actual meaning: vendor/alacritty_terminal/src/term/mod.rs:2209–2213 returns from clipboard_load unless the setting is OnlyPaste or CopyPaste, so OnlyCopy rejects before any ClipboardLoad callback is built/emitted at 2223–2229. SPEC.md Terminal experience requires reads never receive clipboard contents; the replacement refusal is upstream of the browser. This refutes only the changed deletion route and does not audit arbitrary user-initiated paste, clipboard writes, or unrelated read channels. Suggested bucket: other as refuted changed-route security regression; original highest-impact concern preserved. Confidence: confirmed source analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation, not accepted by parent. possible_cover: none searched. Could-be-highest: yes for the original clipboard-exfiltration hypothesis, whose premise is refuted for this replacement path. No readily checkable premise remains unresolved.
